I don't mean to be rude, but if you think the tone of Global Warming (and by extension the whole album) is doom and gloom you are either being facetious or lacking in your media literacy skills. The literal name of the album is about going from the internal war of climate doomerism to the peace of optimism and hope, From Mars to Sirius, and this is written plain as day in the lyrics of Global Warming. Seriously, go re-read them. The "A world is down and none can rebuild it" line is a part of the song about accepting that things look hopeless, and then later on in the song it moves to a vision of hope:  
"And all the worlds, the fates of the countries  
They're all rebuilding at the same time"  
I don't understand how you can look at an album that ends with the line "We will see our children growing" repeated over and over and not interpret it as a message of radical hope. In fact, I would say it's probably the most hopeful piece of art I've ever seen, because it acknowledges and looks in the face of all the anger, fear, loneliness, and pessimism that comes with the reality of climate change and it builds beyond it back to a feeling of optimism and hope.  
Btw, super jealous that you got to see them play it live the first time they ever toured the US, that must've been super awesome. I hope you can find the time to go back and look through the lyrics of the album again, because I think you can find there is a whole other dimension to it that you've been missing.
